title: Single-source activation-ledger command identity
description: Objective: expose the landed activation ledger writer's exact internal command identity so decision-verified readers can reject self-consistent foreign commands without copying a private literal. Deliverable: export one `ACTIVATION_LEDGER_COMMAND_KIND` constant from the existing activation ledger contracts, make `commitActivationLedgerRecord` consume that single source, and pin the real SQLite decision/receipt/event provenance without changing command bytes, event bytes, replay identity, or wire vocabulary. NOT in scope: the attempt-binding reader, runtime command kinds, HTTP registry, schema, lifecycle/history behavior, or new refusal codes. Verification: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` must execute with a nonzero Test Files/Tests count; run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` separately.
definitionOfDone: `activation-ledger-contracts.ts` exports the literal-typed `ACTIVATION_LEDGER_COMMAND_KIND = "activation.commit"`, and production contains no second activation-ledger writer command-kind literal.

`commitActivationLedgerRecord` imports and uses that constant for its decision key while preserving the existing aggregate, command, request, event, payload, result, and replay identities byte-for-byte.

A real SqliteEventStore test commits through the production activation writer and asserts the stored command decision, command receipt, and activation event trace all bind to the exported constant, with a positive stored-event count and exact expected version/result/event identity.

Identical replay returns the original durable bytes with unchanged raw event and decision counts; a compile-preserving wrong-kind production mutation reddens the named provenance assertion before restoration.
Daemon typecheck and daemon tests execute successfully with nonzero test counts, and completion names task-7e3ede6c76324017a1d53601940391f0 as the consumer.

This is an internal single-source refactor, not a new RuntimeCommandKind or wire/registry command; preserve all durable identity bytes and existing stable refusal codes/layers.
Keep both production files at or below 250 physical lines and use TDD exact production-surface assertions; generated/stored cases must prove a positive count.
Run daemon gates separately, commit only explicit owned paths, and record task-7e3ede6c76324017a1d53601940391f0 as the real consumer.

Before writing assertions I ran a throwaway probe INSIDE the owned test file (never a new path, so task rail 1 was not widened) that committed through `commitActivationLedgerRecord` against a real file-backed SqliteEventStore and dumped the durable decision, receipt and event. All five plan goldens reproduce exactly at HEAD 93e17b4: decisionId `1e0590dd…e91dda`, decision requestSha256 `5b7ecc51…f9b450b`, event/receipt requestSha256 `732eaf14…232029dc`, effectSha256 `dfbae727…2b88b208`, resultSha256 `0289b674…453a2a4e`. The probe was removed in the same step; the file now contains only real assertions.

ONE PLAN DETAIL THE PROBE CORRECTED, and it would have produced a false test. `store.getCommandReceipt("command-1")` — the caller's own commandId — returns NULL. The receipt is keyed by the store's INTERNAL effect command id, `moe-internal:decision-effect:<decisionId>`, which is the value the stored event carries in `event.commandId`. A test that had asserted a receipt under the caller's key would have failed for a reason unrelated to this task, or worse, been written as an optional-chained no-op. So the receipt is now fetched via `event.commandId`, and the null under the caller's key is asserted explicitly as the fact it is.

THREE NEW CASES, in a second `describe("activation ledger command identity")`:
1. Literal + type ratchet: `expect(ACTIVATION_LEDGER_COMMAND_KIND).toBe("activation.commit")` plus `expectTypeOf<typeof …>().toEqualTypeOf<"activation.commit">()`. The daemon tsconfig includes `src/**/*.ts`, so the type ratchet is enforced by `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck`, not merely decorative — a widening to `string` reds the gate.
2. Provenance over a real reopened-file store: singleton positive event count, then `decision.commandKind` and `event.decisionTrace.commandKind` both bound to the exported constant, EFFECTS_COMMITTED with expected/observed/previous 0 -> current 1, targetAggregateId = DERIVED, businessEventIds `[grant-0001]`, empty outbox, `decision.resultBytes` byte-equal to `event.payload`, all four decision-side goldens, event type/id/aggregate/sequence/requestSha256, and the receipt bound through `event.commandId` with eventIds, versions, effectSha256 and requestSha256.
3. Replay: raw store-wide counts via `readEventsAfter(0n,100)` / `readCommandDecisionsAfter(0n,100)`, asserted POSITIVE (1 and 1) before the replay so "unchanged" is a real comparison rather than 0 === 0, then identical-input replay -> disposition REPLAYED, byte-identical payload and decisionSha256, unchanged counts.

ANTI-TAUTOLOGY, stated because this is the risk the plan flagged. Comparing the durable kind only to the exported constant would stay green if both moved together. Three independent things stop that: the literal ratchet pins the constant to the string itself; the type ratchet stops it widening; and `commandKind` is hashed into the store's request identity (`identifyExpectedVersionRequest`), so any change to the string moves `decisionId` and the decision `requestSha256` — and those goldens were measured against the writer BEFORE the constant existed, so they provably were not produced by it. I also asserted `receipt.requestSha256` NOT equal to `decision.requestSha256`: they are different digest domains over different inputs, and one hash asserted for both would pass while the writer bound the wrong one.

DRILL HARNESS: python, run from a script OUTSIDE the repo (AppData\Local\Temp) so no scratch file can reach a commit. Binary `read_bytes`/`write_bytes` only — `write_text` rewrites LF as CRLF on Windows and a restore then differs by every line ending while git may still read clean. Restore is in `finally` and proven by SHA-256, not by git status. vitest output captured as BYTES and decoded utf-8 explicitly; `text=True` decodes cp1252 here and eats the lines naming the failing tests. The harness also asserts its anchor was FOUND and counts occurrences, so a drill that applied nothing cannot read as green.

DRILL 1 — wrong kind at the writer, export left correct. `commandKind: ACTIVATION_LEDGER_COMMAND_KIND` -> `commandKind: "work.resume"` (compile-preserving; the store field is typed `string`). anchor occurrences=1, EXIT=1, `2 failed | 14 passed (16)`.
  `AssertionError: expected 'work.resume' to be 'activation.commit'`
  RED: "binds the stored decision, receipt and event trace to the exported command kind"
  RED: "replays the identical command without adding a raw event or decision row"
The literal-ratchet test stayed GREEN, which is the correct discrimination — the constant was not touched. This is the proof the provenance test is not a constant compared to itself: the constant was right and the durable row disagreed.

DRILL 2 — wrong value at the export, so writer and constant move TOGETHER. This is the vacuity the plan named as risk one. `3 failed | 13 passed (16)`, EXIT=1, first `AssertionError: expected 'activation.committed' to be 'activation.commit'`. All three new tests red.

THE DEFECT THE DRILLS FOUND. On the first run, DRILL 2 produced only 2 REDs — the replay test SURVIVED it. I dumped the full vitest output rather than accepting the pass, and the cause is a fact I had asserted without measuring: I claimed in step 2 that changing the command kind moves `decisionId`. IT DOES NOT. Measured: mutating the export moves the decision `requestSha256` from `5b7ecc51…` to `be96c146…`, and the provenance test reds on that line — but `decisionId` is unchanged, because it is derived from the decision KEY (projectId, principalId, commandId), not from the request. My replay test pinned only `decisionId` plus two constant-to-constant comparisons, so it was structurally blind to the exact drift this task exists to prevent while looking identity-bound.
FIX: the replay test now also pins `decisionsAfter[0].requestSha256` to the decision-domain golden and `eventsAfter[0].requestSha256` to the effect-domain golden. Re-run: DRILL 2 now reds all three tests. The GOLDEN doc comment was corrected too — it previously stated the false decisionId claim in the code itself.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) Let task-7e3ede6c copy the private string `activation.commit` into its new reader. Rejected: two protocol literals can drift, letting a writer change while the reader keeps granting stale authority. 2) Verify only decision/receipt self-consistency without checking decision.commandKind. Rejected: a self-consistent foreign command could then mint an activation-shaped event that passes the reader. 3) Expand RuntimeCommandKind or the HTTP registry. Rejected: this identity is an existing internal durable writer kind, not a wire command. 4) Export the existing literal from the focused activation contracts and consume it in the writer.
